subject: SIG follow-up: VPC handshake, PrivateLink option and egress IP evidence
messages:
From: Adam Brewer <adam.brewer@blueriverhealth.com>

Cc: security_ops@blueriverhealth.com
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: SIG follow-up — network details we still need

Evelyn,

Thanks for taking SIG earlier this week. A couple of follow-ups from our security team so we can close the network section:

- Do you support VPC peering or only PrivateLink / interface endpoints for the hosted offering? If both, please call out which deployment modes they apply to (hosted, dedicated, private).
- For PrivateLink / managed endpoints we need the exact service name and whether customers get regional interface endpoints (us-east-1).
- Provide the list of public egress IPs (by region) used for callbacks and webhook traffic so we can add them to our allowlist. We also need NAT gateway IPs for Dedicated/Private setups if different.
- Confirm ephemeral port ranges and any TLS termination/inspection recommendations for our infra team.

Attach any diagrams, a short one-page summary, and a csv of IP ranges if possible. Our target for SIG closure is next Monday.

Appreciate it,
Adam
Adam Brewer
Security Architect | BlueRiver Health
adam.brewer@blueriverhealth.com

Hi Adam — thanks, and good questions. Quick summary up front, followed by next steps and attachments to follow once infra confirms exact egress IPs: 

Summary answers (short):
- Deployment modes:
  * Private deployment (VPC/on‑prem): Full VPC peering or customer-controlled routing — yes, we support direct peering for self-hosted packages and private control-plane installs.
  * Dedicated (reserved capacity): We can offer VPC peering or transit connectivity depending on contract; many customers use interface endpoints for minimal config.
  * Hosted API (public): We do provide AWS PrivateLink (interface endpoints) for enterprise customers who require private connectivity to the hosted control plane — this is region-specific (we support us-east-1 today).
- PrivateLink/service name: We will include the exact service name and implementation notes in the follow-up doc.
- Egress IPs / NAT: Infra is pulling precise NAT/egress ranges by region — Karthik and Diego are on this.
- Ephemeral ports / TLS: Default ephemeral port range we recommend is 32768–61000; we terminate TLS at our edge for hosted; for Private/Dedicated customers we hand control of TLS certs to the customer unless otherwise agreed.

Next steps: Diego will produce a short topology diagram, a CSV of egress ranges, and a one-page SIG evidence summary that you can attach to the questionnaire. Can you confirm whether you need presigned evidence links (Drive) or a zipped package delivered via HubSpot/DocuSign?

I'll follow up once infra confirms the lists — target by EOD Thu PST.

Thanks,
Evelyn Hart
Head of Customer Security Programs | Redwood Inference
Evelyn.Hart@redwoodinference.com

1) A one-page topology diagram called redwood_vpc_handshake_diagram_blueRiver.pdf that shows: PrivateLink interface endpoint behavior for hosted, peering topology for Private, and where NAT egress would sit for Dedicated.
2) Exact public egress IP set for us-east-1 (csv) and a concise paragraph on whether those IPs are stable or periodically rotated.
3) Ephemeral port ranges and any recommended firewall rules; note if TLS is terminated at our edge vs customer-managed for each deployment mode.

Can you deliver drafts by EOD Thu? Adam is looking to close the SIG early next week.

Thanks,
Karthik

Karthik / Evelyn — attaching the requested artifacts and pasting the key details inline for quick review. Attachments are stubs listed in the ticket: redwood_vpc_handshake_diagram_blueRiver.pdf, egress_ips_us-east-1.csv, privatelink_configuration_notes.docx.

Key details (for inclusion in SIG response):
- Hosted (Public Redwood API) -> PrivateLink: Supported in regions where we operate dedicated interface endpoints (us-east-1). Service name: com.redwoodinference.us-east-1.api. Customers requesting PrivateLink are provisioned an interface endpoint in their VPC that forwards to our private NLBs.

- Dedicated -> VPC Peering / Transit: For Dedicated customers we support VPC peering or transit gateway attachments depending on topology. In most Dedicated installs, NAT egress is sourced from managed NAT gateways owned by Redwood – we provide the egress IPs for allowlisting.

- Private (VPC/on‑prem package) -> Customer controls egress: In private deployments the customer typically manages NAT and egress IPs. Redwood will document recommended NAT IPs and can run through a handoff process where we confirm the final allowlist entries.

Egress IPs (us-east-1) — current active list (subject to scheduled maintenance rotations; we publish changes at least 72 hours in advance):
- 34.201.125.48
- 34.201.125.49
- 34.201.125.50
- 34.201.125.51
(see egress_ips_us-east-1.csv for machine-readable format and CIDR mappings)

Ephemeral ports: 32768–61000 (recommended).

TLS: Hosted — TLS terminated at Redwood edge NLB (mutual TLS available on request for dedicated flows). Dedicated/Private — we recommend customer-managed certs; Redwood can support TLS passthrough or termination per contract.

Stability: The egress IPs above are stable for 90+ days during normal operations. Planned rotations will be communicated via the Drive folder and HubSpot deal notes.

I'll attach the files to Evelyn's reply to Adam once you sign off.

Diego
Senior Network Engineer | Redwood Inference
